position: Parental Rights in Education (and New Agency Policies)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress pass a federal Parents' Bill of Rights requiring strict scrutiny when federal action infringes parental rights, and amend FERPA and PPRA to give parents a private right of action for injunctive and declaratory relief with attorneys' fees. It also recommends that ED be transparent about FERPA and PPRA complaints, build a parent portal explaining those rights, and state that FERPA gives parents full access to their children's education records.
remaining: Enactment of a Parents' Bill of Rights with a strict scrutiny standard.

A parent portal and published complaint data from ED, if pursued.

status_summary: The legislative core is introduced only: the Families' Rights and Responsibilities Act (S. 204 and House companion H.R. 650, both introduced 2025-01-23 and referred to the Judiciary committees) would apply strict scrutiny to government burdens on parental rights, and the Parental Rights Relief Act (H.R. 6860, introduced 2025-12-18) would create a private right of action under FERPA and PPRA for declaratory and injunctive relief and fees; the bill status records for all three bills show no action after introduction and referral. One administrative item is met: ED's Student Privacy Policy Office announced a Dear Colleague letter on 2025-03-28 stating that parents must be able to review all education records, required state agencies to document compliance by 2025-04-30 and opened FERPA investigations of the California and Maine education departments; on 2026-10-05 ED and DOJ told state attorneys general that FERPA and PPRA funding conditions are non-negotiable. ED's complaint page still uses a PDF form sent by email or mail, and no new parent portal or public complaint reporting was found, so the stage is proposed.

timeline.event: The Families' Rights and Responsibilities Act was introduced as S. 204 (Senator Tim Scott; read twice and referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee) with House companion H.R. 650 (Representative Foxx; referred to the House Judiciary Committee); it declares parental rights fundamental and bars substantial government burdens unless they meet strict scrutiny.
ED announced a Dear Colleague letter on FERPA and PPRA, a 2025-04-30 documentation deadline for state agencies, and FERPA investigations of the California and Maine education departments.

H.R. 6860, the Parental Rights Relief Act, was introduced and referred to the House Education and Workforce Committee; it would let parents and eligible students sue for declaratory or injunctive relief and fees under FERPA and PPRA without exhausting administrative remedies, and require ED to resolve complaints within 90 days.

ED and DOJ sent state attorneys general a letter calling FERPA and PPRA funding conditions non-negotiable and requiring written parental consent for mental health screenings, with joint PPRA investigations opened in July still pending.
